subject: science

applicable_programme.grade_mapping_note: The public PYP page describes the programme as education for children aged 3-12. Mapping that span to Grade 5 (often about ages 10-11) is our convention, not an IB grade boundary.

grade_specific_note.label: C
grade_specific_note.text: Grade 5 Florida science includes controlled experiments, forms of energy and closed circuits, the Solar System, climate zones, and a recognition that matter is made of parts too small to see. That is more specified than the public PYP overview and should stay labeled as Florida content.

subject_group_or_structure.mapping_to_primer_subject: The grade 3 library says PYP does not keep science as a separate subject and explores it through themes, especially How the world works and Sharing the planet. Public pages support transdisciplinary themes and subject-specific learning. The four science strand names below are reused from that grade 3 file.

concepts: Causation - Why is it like it is?
Connection - How is it connected to other things?
Perspective - What are the points of view?
global_contexts_or_transdisciplinary_the: Where we are in place and time

official_requirements.label: B
official_requirements.text: The programme of inquiry is organized and framed by six transdisciplinary themes: Who we are; Where we are in place and time; How we express ourselves; How the world works; How we organize ourselves; Sharing the planet.

official_requirements.label: B
official_requirements.text: Although subjects play an important role in learning, PYP learners explore real-world problems by going beyond subject boundaries.

official_requirements.label: B
official_requirements.text: PYP Science scope and sequence, as recorded in the grade 3 library, covers four strands: Living things, Earth and space, Materials and matter, and Forces and energy.

typical_fit.label: C
typical_fit.text: Grade 5 Florida science in this draft has students plan investigations with variables and a control group, investigate energy, electricity, and forces, identify human organs and adaptations, describe galaxies and the Solar System, model the water cycle and climate, and compare properties of matter. Those NGSSS benchmarks can be inquired into under How the world works and Sharing the planet. They are not IB learning outcomes.

suggested_alignment_to_florida_and_arizo.label: C

florida.alignment_note: Defining a problem and carrying out investigations fits inquiry and research skills. The Florida list of investigation types is the requirement.
Explaining that science is grounded in testable observations fits thinking skills. It is not a published PYP phase outcome.
Basic forms of energy, including light, heat, sound, electrical, chemical, and mechanical, fit the reused Forces and energy strand.
Adaptations that help plants and animals survive in different environments fit Living things and can connect to Sharing the planet.
Distinguishing the Sun, planets, moons, asteroids, and comets, and identifying Earth's position, fits the reused Earth and space strand.
Comparing solids, liquids, and gases by properties such as mass, volume, color, texture, and temperature fits Materials and matter.

suggested_alignment_to_florida_and_arizo.notes: Arizona standards deferred. These rows are suggested starting points (Label C), not an official IB-Florida crosswalk.
